1.e4 e6 2.d4 a6 3.Nf3 b5 4.Bd3 c5 5.c3 B.strategy: Gets the king to safety before the centre opens. With Black's bishop already aimed at e4 and the d4 pawn under pressure, White wants the king out of the middle and a rook developed, while the bishop and the pawn chain hold the centre together for now.

Brings out the last minor piece with a point: e4 is now attacked twice, by bishop and knight, and defended once, so White has to defend or advance the pawn at once. Black develops while keeping the initiative against the white centre and the space gained on the queenside.
1.e4 e6 2.d4 a6 3.Nf3 b5 4.Bd3 c5 5.c3 B.name: French Defence: St. George Defence, Traditional Line
